reasons: Split into engine (logic) and cli (interface) to allow parallel development and independent testing of core logic vs argument parsing.

items.title: Engine Tests
items.goal: Define tests for the calculation engine

card.context: The engine provides a single function to evaluate arithmetic expressions.
card.contract: Function: double evaluate(const std::string& expr). Supports +, -, *, /, parentheses. Returns NaN on error (invalid syntax, division by zero). No side effects.

card.context: Implement the logic defined in the contract.
card.contract: Implement double evaluate(const std::string& expr) declared in include/calc/engine.hpp. Must handle basic arithmetic with correct precedence and parentheses. Return NaN for any error.
acceptance: every test in the tester's file passes

items.title: CLI Tests
items.goal: Define tests for the command-line interface

card.context: The CLI takes an expression from command line args and prints the result.
card.contract: Function: int run(const std::vector<std::string>& args). Expects exactly one arg: the expression. Prints result to stdout (formatted as double) and returns 0. If args count != 1, prints usage to stderr and returns 1. If evaluation fails, prints error to stderr and returns 1.
acceptance: Usage error for too many args

card.context: Implement the main function and run wrapper.
card.contract: Implement int run(const std::vector<std::string>& args) declared in include/calc/cli.hpp (or inline in main if preferred, but plan assumes header). Calls evaluate from engine. Formats output. Handles errors.
acceptance: every test in the tester's file passes
